summary: Wisconsin has no sale or closing requirement, but the owner of every one- or two-family home has a standing duty to have working smoke alarms and carbon monoxide alarms in the basement and on each floor, no matter how old the house is.
alarmType: Smoke detectors: the owner must install a functional detector in the basement and on each floor level, except the attic or storage area, of each dwelling unit; detectors must be approved and installed and maintained as required under the residential-building provisions. No power source is specified for smoke detectors in the statute text read. CO detectors: must bear an Underwriters Laboratories listing mark, may be combined with a smoke detector, and must be installed per the manufacturer's directions in the basement and on each floor level except the attic, garage, or storage area of each dwelling unit; a hardwired unit must have a backup battery. For homes whose initial-construction building permit issued on or after February 1, 2011 and that take electric service from a public utility, each CO detector must be powered by the home's electrical wiring.
coAlarms: Yes, under their own statute and applying to one- and two-family homes regardless of when they were built. Exempt: a home with no attached garage, no fireplace, and no fuel-burning appliance. The occupant normally maintains the detector; if a non-owner occupant or an authorized inspector gives the owner written notice a detector is not working, the owner has 5 days to fix it. Tampering with or removing an installed detector or its batteries is prohibited.
citation: Wis. Stat. § 101.645 (smoke detectors in dwellings) with § 101.615 (applies regardless of when construction commenced) and § 101.61(1) (dwelling = building with one or 2 dwelling units); Wis. Stat. § 101.647 (carbon monoxide detectors in dwellings); Wis. Stat. §§ 101.145 and 101.149 (smoke and CO detectors in residential buildings used for lodging - not one- or two-family homes)
lastAmended: § 101.647 created by 2009 Wisconsin Act 158, eff. February 1, 2011. §§ 101.615 and 101.645 as amended by 1989 Wisconsin Act 109, eff. December 20, 1989. Any amendment after those dates was not checked.

Amendments to §§ 101.615, 101.645 or 101.647 after those acts were not checked, so the wording may have changed.

1989 Act 109 itself contains an inconsistency: its amendment to § 101.645 refers to dwellings whose construction commenced on or after May 23, 1978, while the new § 101.615 it creates says § 101.645 applies to dwellings commenced before, on, or after May 23, 1978. The current statute should be re-read to settle which controls.
